playbook:
When hide stage opens and I'm alive, pick a central cell (5) on the first round unless I have a specific late-game reason to bias elsewhere.

When I'm hit, do not automatically abandon station: generally hold position after a single isolated hit to avoid signaling; move off my previous hide to an adjacent cell (±1) only if I am hit repeatedly by the same shooter or if the pattern of incoming hits makes my current cell clearly exposed.

When the standing order assigns a target, follow the standing order and target that boat unless a clear tactical reason prevents it (Harbor warning, target already jettisoned, or a coordinated escort/ambush plan is in place).

When choosing a fire cell, prefer to reuse my current hide cell as my shot guess to keep behavior simple and maintain symmetry. If I have accumulated two or more consecutive misses against the same target, vary my shot cell by moving it one step (±1) from the last fired cell to probe adjacent cells rather than repeating identical guesses indefinitely.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, always file the public claim that exactly matches that private result (truthful claim). Truthful claims avoid detectably inconsistent public information and keep options open for future coordination.

Never fire on Harbor by default; only fire on Harbor if I'm explicitly willing to accept the payroll penalty (+3 to me, -3 to Harbor) and the tactical benefit clearly outweighs the cost.

When naming an escort (salvage), only name an actual live picket boat (Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor if alive). Do not invent names; invalid escort claims are pointless and may be disallowed.

When I want escort points, coordinate to create a mutual escort claim with one other live boat (each names the other the same round). If no credible mutual agreement is in place (no prior implicit/explicit coordination), claim none.

When composing public notes, keep them bland and consistent with my chosen station posture (e.g., "steady on station") to avoid signaling deceptive patterns unless I'm attempting a coordinated mutual escort or deception; in that case, make the minimal necessary note to enable coordination.

When I detect an opponent favoring a specific cell (from hits/misses timing or repeated outcomes), bias my subsequent fires against them toward that cell to exploit predictability. Conversely, if opponents hit me repeatedly from one side, consider shifting my hide one cell away in subsequent rounds.

If a line of play (e.g., claiming escorts with nonexistent boats or attempting coordinated moves without reciprocation) fails or is disallowed, stop immediately and revert to valid direct actions: truthful shot claims, valid escort names, and following standing-order targeting.

Prefer minimal, consistent public behavior to avoid creating exploitable signaling unless I have an explicit coordination plan that has been accepted by another live boat.

Adjust thresholds in practice: tolerate one hit before moving; begin varying shot cells after two consecutive misses on the same target; require at least one prior reciprocal verbal or behavioral cue before committing to an escort claim.

1.text:
When asked for hide, pick a cell different from my previous hide; avoid repeating the same hide number across rounds. Prefer central cells early if I have no pattern to exploit, but vary deliberately to prevent opponents learning my sequence.

If opponents have repeatedly targeted my previous hides, shift away from those cells and adopt a small randomized window (±1–2 cells) around a new center rather than a fixed number.

When given the standing-order target, follow it unless there is a clear tactical reason to diverge (e.g., firing on Harbor only if I accept the payroll penalty for an expected decisive gain). By default do not fire on Harbor.

When choosing a firing coordinate, do not reuse the same coordinate repeatedly. Use one of two methods:
- Local probe: if I suspect a particular opponent is aiming at my recent hides, probe a few nearby cells around my current hide in successive rounds to detect clustering.
- Fresh search: if I believe the opponent is spreading, choose a fresh cell each time chosen from a short pseudo-random sequence to avoid predictability.

When I score a hit on a boat, continue to prioritize targeting that boat only if standing order supports it or there is recent evidence their hide remains localized; do not assume the same cell will produce repeated hits—shift search area around that boat and vary shots.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, echo that result publicly exactly (claims must match private result). Do not lie.

When posting a station note, keep it short and noncommittal by default (e.g., "holding position" or "steady on station") to avoid revealing patterns. If I want to encourage mutual escort, use a paired signaling convention (mirror another boat's phrasing) only when I have reason to believe they are willing to reciprocate.

When naming an escort, name another boat only if I have a reasonable expectation they will name me back (based on prior notes, explicit reciprocation, or obvious mutual benefit). If there is uncertainty, claim none. If I detect a clear two-way signaling opportunity, explicitly commit to escort to capture the 5-point bonus.

When a round summary shows repeated misses from a particular opponent at my hide, change hide patterns and avoid returning to recently targeted cells immediately.

Avoid unilateral or false escort claims; they are low-value and risk revealing intentions.

Do not lock into a single firing coordinate across rounds—repeating the same fire number made me predictable and reduced my score. Alternate probes and searches so opponents cannot infer my hides from repeated shots.

If I am tempted to take a high-risk/high-reward action (e.g., firing on Harbor for payroll), calculate the net expected value: include guaranteed jettison penalty (Harbor loses 3 and I gain 3) and likely responses. By default, avoid attacking Harbor unless the EV clearly favors it.

Use station notes intentionally when attempting to coordinate escorts: if I want to set up mutual escort, match wording and timing with a target boat and be prepared to follow through with the salvage claim if reciprocated.

When opponents show persistent behavior (e.g., one boat repeatedly hits another in successive rounds), adjust by targeting positions that exploit that behavior only after confirming they have not moved; otherwise shift focus to opportunities with better expected return.

Keep records mentally (or in-game notes) of which cells I used for hides and shots to avoid accidental repetition and to detect patterns in opponents' fire.

Revise tactics mid-patrol when evidence contradicts my assumptions: if my central-start assumption leads to early predictability (e.g., repeated hits or being targeted), abandon central bias and employ more randomness and local probing.

Prioritize survival and steady point accumulation over speculative gambits; small recurring gains (escort reciprocity, consistent non-Harbor hits) beat a single high-risk play that risks being jettisoned or revealing my pattern.

2.text:
When asked to hide, pick a cell that is not an obvious repeat of my prior hides; alternate between center and an edge and occasionally pick a high/low extreme so my pattern is hard to guess. If I just got hit, change quadrant from my last hide. If I scored a hit on someone in the previous round, bias my next hide away from the quadrant where I think that opponent will look next (to avoid predictable retaliation).

When told the standing order target, fire at that named boat unless there is a compelling tactical reason not to. Do not fire at Harbor unless Harbor has already been forced off the board and the rules allow — firing at Harbor incurs a heavy guaranteed penalty and is not worth it.

When choosing a fire cell against a boat, do not repeat a cell that I fired earlier at the same target if that shot missed. Use past hit/miss history against that target (my own private results and observed public claims) to eliminate cells and bias toward untried cells in the same quadrant as any observed hits.

If I have no information, pick a moderately central cell but vary it enough between rounds to avoid simple predictability (e.g., do not pick the exact same central cell every round). If I previously hit the target on a specific cell, prioritize firing that same cell on the next round against that same target (targets often persist on a hiding cell). If that repeated-fire is followed by a miss, interpret that as the target having moved and then shift to adjacent cells (first try orthogonally adjacent, then diagonals) rather than jumping back to entirely different quadrants.

When I receive my private shot result, always file the required public claim that matches it exactly — truthful claiming is mandatory.

When composing my station note, keep it generic and nonrevealing (e.g., "steady on station") unless I can exploit a predictable opponent reaction: mimic other boats' notes to blend in or use neutral phrasing to avoid giving location hints.

When deciding an escort claim, only claim an escort if I am confident the other boat will reciprocate this round (based on prior mutual behavior). If I cannot reasonably expect reciprocation, claim none — random solo escort claims are wasted opportunities and produce no points. Save escort claims for rounds where a reciprocal pattern has already been established or where making one can lock in a mutual payment.

When I notice another boat repeatedly targeting the same opponent and getting misses, assume they are using a narrow predictable set of cells; exploit that by varying my own firing to different cells to gain hits. Conversely, when an opponent scores a hit on a target, infer the hit cell's neighborhood and try adjacent cells on subsequent attacks against that target.

When my score is behind and there is an opportunity to get a hit by deviating from the standing order, consider breaking order only if the expected gain minus risk (including any Harbor penalty) is favorable. Otherwise follow the standing order to avoid chaotic mistakes. If I repeatedly see that the standing-order target is consistently moving or evading, consider a one-off deviation to exploit a likely stationary alternative target—only when the expected return is clear.

When behavior in prior rounds shows my choices were too predictable (e.g., repeating the same fire cell or hiding spot), explicitly change pattern next decision rather than subtle variation — make a noticeable change sufficient to be nonobvious to opponents.

When I lack information, prioritize survival of points over risky plays: avoid attacking Harbor, avoid making escort claims without reciprocation, and avoid repeating failed shots.

New/updated rules based on recent play:
- If I score a hit on a target, treat that hit cell as the lead hypothesis for the target’s continued hiding spot and fire the same cell at the next opportunity against that target. If that second shot is a miss, treat it as evidence of movement and then try adjacent cells rather than jumping to a distant quadrant.
- If I get a sequence of hits on the same target using the same cell, continue until I detect a miss; this consolidates points quickly when opponent is static.
- If I get an initial hit and the target subsequently changes (hit then miss), prioritize searching nearby cells before abandoning the quadrant entirely — targets tend to shift locally rather than teleporting.
- Maintain truthful public claims without exception; consistency in public claims helps me interpret others’ public claims and infer hiding patterns.
- Do not waste final-round escort claims unless a high-probability reciprocal match is expected; final-round solo claims are opportunity cost without benefit.

When in doubt, prefer conservative pattern variation that preserves earned points while probing for reliable information to convert into repeated hits.

The sea is a line of 9 cells. Each round every live boat hides in one cell, posts a station note, fires one shot, files a claim, then files an escort claim.

ESCORT CLAIMS. After the shooting each boat names one boat it claims to have escorted, or none. Where two boats name each other the office pays each of them 5 POINTS.

Notes are relayed to the whole picket, Harbor included. Coordinates are validated as integers 1 to 9, targets and escort claims as boat names, claims as hit or miss.
